subject: Sealed environment: operational facts, runbook & SLA appendix
messages:
From: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — evidence needed for sealed environment evaluation

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. As part of our security review for an on-prem sealed deployment, the procurement and security teams asked for a concise operational fact summary and a runbook excerpt that speaks to:

- network egress controls (can the runtime operate with zero outbound connections?),
- image/update process for air-gapped sites (signed bundles and offline installation flow),
- operator authentication (KMS/HSM integration, operator key escrow),
- telemetry/telemetry toggle (what is collected by default, and how to turn it off),
- SLA language for patch/critical fix turnaround in isolated environments.

Can you send a short factsheet and a runbook snippet we can include in our RFP pack? Procurement would like this by EOD Monday so we can include it in the vendor scoring worksheet.

Also, any sample wording for an SLA appendix that clarifies responsibilities during offline upgrades would be very helpful.

Best,
Sandra
Sandra Lee
Director, Platform Security
Acme Health

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence needed for sealed environment evaluation

Sandra — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise factsheet and a runbook extract that maps directly to each ask. High-level notes up front:

- Zero egress: our runtime supports fully isolated operation when using the sealed bundle delivery and operator toolset — no outbound connections required for inference if KV cache is local and model artifacts are preloaded.
- Offline updates: we provide digitally signed bundle artifacts (PKCS7 signatures) that your operators can stage and install via the operator CLI; an attest file and checksum accompany each bundle.
- Operator auth: supports HSM-backed keys (PKCS11) and customer-managed KMS. We recommend operator keys be stored in HSM-backed secrets and use short-lived operator sessions.
- Telemetry: default install collects basic health metrics only; telemetry is disabled by default in sealed mode. We include an explicit telemetry toggle in the operator runbook.
- SLA for offline sites: proposed appendix covers critical-fix delivery windows, on-site operator phone support, and optional on-site engineer dispatch. See attached SLA appendix draft.

Attachments: redwood_sealed_ops_factsheet_v1.pdf (2 pages), runbook-extract-sealed-env.docx (operator steps, 6 pages).

Action items:
1) Review factsheet with security and let us know any gaps.
2) If approved, we can add an additional page that maps controls to your internal control IDs (e.g., ACME-SEC-*) for procurement scoring.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence needed for sealed environment evaluation

Looping in Marissa for any notes on operator training and certification that we should include in the runbook extract. Two questions I want answered before we finalize:

1) HSM integration specifics — which PKCS11 vendors/configurations have we validated? (Acme uses Thales nShield and Azure Dedicated HSM).
2) Upgrade rollback — the runbook mentions a two-stage upgrade with canary on a shadow node. For truly isolated single-node installs, what is the rollback story? Need precise steps and expected RTO for the SLA appendix.

Short replies welcome — Sandra wants this in the purchase packet by Tuesday.

— Priyom

From: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence needed for sealed environment evaluation

Jasmine — the materials look good at a glance. Procurement has two procurement-specific asks:

- Can you produce a short SLA appendix (1 page) that we can attach to the MSA that spells out: patch windows for critical vulnerability notification (T+24), emergency hotfix delivery timing (target T+72), and an explicit statement of responsibilities for the customer during offline installs?
- Can you provide a sample procurement checklist (one-page) listing what we must provide for an isolated site go-live (operator contact, hardware baseline, storage manifest, signed bundle ingestion instructions)?

If you can get the SLA appendix PDF and the checklist by EOD today we can include them in the vendor pack for the security scoring meeting.

Regards,
Sandra

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence needed for sealed environment evaluation

Sandra — attached: SLA appendix (sla-appendix-acme-20261020.pdf) and a one-page procurement checklist (inline below). I also added short clarifications to Priyom's questions:

- HSM: we have validated PKCS11 integration with Thales nShield (v2.0+) and Azure Dedicated HSM. Integration notes are in the runbook extract (step 3.2). For other vendors we provide a PKCS11 shim guide; our engineering team will validate a customer test key during pilot.
- Rollback/Single-node: for single-node sealed installs the recommended rollback is: restore from locally-staged backup snapshot (we include a snapshot/restore helper in the operator toolkit), roll back runtime bundle to previous signed bundle, restart runtime with prior model artifact; typical RTO 60-90 minutes for standard config. The SLA appendix includes an RTO target for rollback-assisted recoveries for the sealed configuration.

Procurement checklist (one-page summary):
- Operator contact (name/email/phone) and designated backup
- Hardware manifest (CPU/GPU, disk/IO baseline, NICs and MTU)
- Storage manifest (model artifact sizes, expected growth)
- HSM/KMS contact and PKCS11 test credentials for pilot (or placeholder for on-site test)
- Signed bundle ingestion procedure acceptance (signed acceptance form)
- Local NTP and CA cert chain ready on operator host

Attachments (sent): sla-appendix-acme-20261020.pdf (1 page), procurement-checklist-acme-20261020.pdf (1 page)

Let me know if security or procurement need additional mapping to ACME control IDs — we can produce a table by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
